subject: Nariway Signals - 2026-09-06 - A 198-year-old museum runs out of runway
html:
The Academy of Natural Sciences closes for good after 198 years, with no plan yet for 19 million specimens — plus a Nazi-era Pissarro claim against the Met, Frieze Masters built around two collectors' houses, and where Alina's referral rooms stand this month.
Nariway Signals September 6, 2026
 
Heaviest today on institutions that have simply run out of runway — a 198-year-old Philadelphia natural history museum announcing it will close for good in three weeks with no plan yet for its 19 million specimens, on the same day Germany's regional elections put public arts funding at real political risk — bracketed by a Nazi-era Pissarro claim reaching a Paris court against the Met, and Frieze Masters building a new fair section around what a collector's own house can preserve that a museum sometimes cannot.
Lead
The Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University will close permanently on Sept 27, after 198 years, with no confirmed future home for its 19 million specimens.
Philadelphia's oldest natural history museum — older than the Smithsonian — is shutting its doors for good later this month; a sale of the building itself is reportedly under consideration, and no public plan yet exists for where the collection goes next. It's the starkest version this brief has tracked of the question sitting underneath every founder-museum success story: for every Lucas or Gochman collection converting itself into permanent public infrastructure, there is a much older, much larger public collection quietly running out of the money to stay open at all, with nobody yet holding the pen on what happens to what's inside.

extinctmonsters.net · New York Almanack
 
What's happening
Germany's regional elections today could reshape public funding for the museums caught in the middle.
Directors at institutions including Kunstmuseum Magdeburg and Bauhaus Dessau are warning that an AfD win in Saxony-Anhalt's Sept 6 vote would put state arts budgets and programming independence at real risk — the policy-and-tax beat this brief tracks, playing out in an election happening as this brief goes out. The Art Newspaper
The Art Gallery of Ontario has set the mechanics of Stephan Jost's succession.
The AGO says it will name an interim director before opening a global search once Jost departs Dec 31 — a concrete governance answer arriving weeks after the museum's own Nan Goldin acquisition dispute triggered board resignations, the donor-intent fight this brief flagged Sept 5. The Art Newspaper
V&A East Museum and Storehouse went dark Sept 4–5 as PCS members struck over pay.
The two-day walkout closed the East London sites (plus Young V&A) while South Kensington and the Schiaparelli show stayed open — the same union whose 95% strike vote this brief logged Aug 30, now actually on the picket line, right as the V&A's East expansion is meant to be scaling up new public collection space. Museums + Heritage · Arts Professional
Frieze Masters is building an entire fair section around two collectors' houses instead of galleries.
"Reflections," curated by Abby Bangser for the Oct 14–18 fair, sets works and design objects inside the sensibility of Casa Luis Barragán in Mexico City and the Cosmic House, the London home Charles and Maggie Jencks built as a total work of art — a major fair explicitly arguing a collector's own domestic space can be as complete a legacy statement as a museum wing. Frieze
James Turrell's newest Ganzfeld work just opened at Superblue Miami, the venture's fifth acquisition since launch.
"Blue Sea Sky" arrives as Superblue — Pace Gallery's for-profit immersive-art spinoff — marks five years running a genuinely different model from the nonprofit founder-museum this brief tracks daily: permanent, purpose-built, commercially operated space built around major living artists' large-scale work. Artnet · ARTnews
 
Worth reading
Marion Maneker on the slow-motion breakup of S.I. Newhouse's collection at Christie's (Puck, "Wall Power").
A blow-by-blow of the Condé Nast chairman's collection being sold off in tranches nearly a decade after his death — the untidy, multi-year reality behind every "estate sale" headline this brief tracks, worth revisiting as a case study in what actually happens when nobody decided in advance. Puck · follow-up
Grant Pierrus, "Why I'm Getting Calls from Billionaires About Contemporary Craft" (On Collecting).
An advisor's own account of ultra-wealthy clients moving serious money into craft and design objects — a live data point on how the definition of "collectible" is shifting for exactly the collectors who will eventually face the legacy question this brief tracks. On Collecting
 
For the record
Seven heirs of a Jewish collector are suing the Met in a French court over a Pissarro, arguing a 1941 sale was made under Nazi-era duress.
The heirs of Max Braunthal say the forced sale is void under a 2023 French law; the Met disputes the claim and maintains fair value was paid at the time. Another entry in the restitution-to-ownership-dispute pipeline this brief tracks — this one testing whether a foreign court can reach into a major US museum's permanent collection at all. ARTnews
 
To see — escalating
Christie's Alan Medaugh Hiroshige preview is now 5 days out — inside one week.
Public preview Sept 11–14, sale Sept 15, 20 Rockefeller Plaza; already on Alina's calendar for the Sept 12 preview. ARTnews
The Bartos Mondrian's Paris leg opens in 3 days; the free New York leg is now 11 days out.
Public-view legs: Paris Sept 9–12, New York Sept 17–20, Hong Kong Sept 25–29, London from Oct 8, sale Oct 14 (£20–30M / $27–41M estimate). ARTnews
Sotheby's Open House (Sept 20–21, Sotheby's NYC HQ) is now 14 days out — inside the ~3-week window.
Its confirmed program includes a session on legal considerations across an art collection's lifecycle, staged by the house's own trusts-and-estates practice. Sotheby's
 
Rooms to be in
Next up: EPC of Westchester County's Fall Networking Event, Sept 23, Freebird Kitchen & Bar, 5pm — 17 days out.
Non-members explicitly welcome (~$85), the lowest-pressure first visit to any of the four target councils. epcwc.org
